title: Genter reader
description: A format reader: data that turns a document's text into its own date, status and explicit marks (replaced, deprecated, removed, with the place that replaces it). It is never run: src/readers.js interprets it. A pattern is a restricted language: literals, '.', classes ([a-z], [^)], \d \s \w and their capitals), anchors (^ $ \b), groups ((...) and (?:...)) and alternation, and bounded repeats (? {n} {n,m}, m at most 200) of something that holds no repeat; no *, +, {n,}, backreference or lookaround. It is matched without case, one trimmed line (at most 400 characters) at a time, in time linear in the line.

dsl.description: The version of this manifest language.

name.description: The name of the reader's folder in readers/.

owner.description: The GitHub handle of the person or organization that keeps it.

fallback.description: true for a reader of any document of a kind (banners, front matter): format readers are asked first.

records.description: true for a reader of decision records (ADRs, RFCs, PEPs, proposals): every document it reads a date, a status or a mark in, or each of its entries for a decision log, is a decision (the decisions page lists it, bench/repos counts it). Not with fallback.

lines.description: How many lines of a document it reads, from the first (60 when not given).

group.description: The number of a group of the pattern, from 1.

where.description: front-matter: the lines between a first line '---' and the next '---'; top: the first `first` lines that are not empty (6 when not given), after the front matter; section: the lines under the first heading `section` matches, to the next heading of its level or above; any: every line read; heading: the headings (an entry's own heading, in an entry). Lines in code fences are never read.

files.description: Globs from the project's root, without case: * and ? within a name, ** for any folders, {a,b} for either. A name that starts with '.' is never matched, and a glob that could match a secret-looking file (*.pem, *.key, id_rsa, credentials) is refused.

headings.description: When given, the reader takes only a document with a heading one of these patterns matches.

phrases.description: Mark a short line with the phrases of the language rules (rules/<lang>.json) instead of a pattern.

id.description: The group that holds the id of what replaces the document (470 in 'Superseded-By: 470'), with `place`: letters, digits and -, at most 32.

place.description: Where the document an id names is, from the marked document's folder: a file's name, after folders ('..' first, at most 3); {id} is the id as written, {id:0N} the id as a number N digits wide (zero first), and * in the file's name any characters. 'pep-{id:04}.*' with 470 is pep-0470.*. The engine takes the one file of the project there that it reads, never an address or a hidden or secret-looking file, else none.

date.description: The first rule that finds a date (its group `value`, 1 when not given) gives it.

status.description: The first rule that finds a status word gives it.

marks.description: Each line it marks, with the replacing place from the group `by` (else a link beside the match), its name from `name`, and, from the group `id`, the place `place` makes of it.

heading.description: An entry is a heading the first of these matches (at its level, when given), to the next heading of its level or above.
